text: The paint led along the cliff path, under the headland, to a door set into the rock.
Thirty years. Gus had walked past it every single day.
No handle. No keyhole. Four brass marks, worn smooth, in a square.
Mabel sniffed the gap under it. Then she sat down very fast, which she only does for two things.
Gus had seen those four marks once before. In a story. One his grandmother used to tell to make children behave.
